judgment.rationale: Both are Primary One Performance Objectives under the same Topic '2. Two dimensional shapes' (Sub-Theme Shapes). The second SFI (Objective 2: match and name a square, a rectangle and a circle) develops recognition and naming of these shapes; the first SFI (Objective 3: distinguish between squares and rectangles) requires learners to already recognize and name those shapes before comparing/contrasting their properties. Same grade rank (0), but the substantive skill dependency (recognition preceding differentiation) justifies the developmental direction rather than mere shared hierarchy or wording overlap.

judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY TWO Performance Objectives under the identical Topic '1. Three dimensional shapes' (Theme: Mensuration and Geometry; Sub-Theme: Shapes). The first asks pupils to mention 3D home objects that are cylinders and spheres; the second asks pupils to identify 3D home objects that are cuboids and cubes. These are parallel, complementary shape-recognition skills applied to different 3D solids in the same home context, giving substantive conceptual coherence. judgment.rationale: First objective 'identify number of objects in a group or collection' (Topic 1, Whole numbers 1-5) is a foundational counting/quantification skill; second objective 'use idea of place value limited to tens and units' (Topic 4, Whole number 10) requires understanding of grouping and counting objects into units and tens. Both sit under the same PRIMARY ONE / NUMBER AND NUMERATION / Whole Number scope (rank 0), and topic ordering (1 before 4) plus the conceptual dependency of place value on prior counting/grouping proficiency supports a lower-to-higher developmental direction from first to second. Shared ancestors and token overlap ('of','the','pupils should be able to') alone are not sufficient, but the substantive counting-to-place-value progression justifies buildsTowards.

judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY THREE Performance Objectives within the Mensuration and Geometry / Primary Measures section dealing with length measurement: the first finds perimeters of regular figures in metres and centimetres by measurement (Topic 2. Length), the second compares non-standard measures such as arm's length (Topic 3. Length II). They share genuine conceptual coherence around measuring length (LC tags 'length'/'measurement' overlap). However, developmental direction is materially ambiguous: comparing non-standard measures is conceptually more foundational, which would suggest second_to_first, yet the source topic ordering places Length (perimeter, standard units) before Length II, contradicting a clean dependency. With same grade rank (0 gap) and no decisive dependency evidence, symmetric relatesTo best fits the substantive length-measurement coherence without asserting a build direction.

producer_judgment.rationale: Both are Performance Objectives under the same PRIMARY TWO Topic '2. Length'. The second SFI (objective 2) has pupils identify differences in arm's length and other body parts used for measurement, i.e. recognizing that non-standard body-based units vary. The first SFI (objective 3) has pupils use metres and centimetres as standard measuring units. Recognizing the variability/inconsistency of body-based measures conceptually motivates and supports adopting standardized units, so proficiency in the second supports success in the first (second_to_first). Same-rank direction is justified by this substantive conceptual progression from non-standard awareness to standard-unit use, not merely by shared topic or numbering.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary One Performance Objectives under the same Topic 'Two dimensional shapes' (Sub-Theme Shapes). Second SFI (c51a279b) asks pupils to 'match and name a square, a rectangle and a Circle' — a foundational recognition/naming skill (LCs: match, name shapes). First SFI (a61e1ae6) asks pupils to 'mention square, rectangular and circular shapes in homes' — an application of that recognition to real-world/home contexts (LCs: mention square/circular/rectangular shapes in homes). Proficiency in naming and matching these shapes plausibly supports success in identifying and mentioning the same shapes in the home environment, so the naming/matching objective builds toward the applied objective (second_to_first). Same grade rank (0), but the applied extension gives substantive same-rank directional evidence beyond shared hierarchy and word overlap.

judgment.rationale: First is a PRIMARY ONE Basic Operations/Addition objective ('add two whole numbers from 1 to 3 with sum less than 5'); second is a PRIMARY ONE Algebraic Processes/Open Sentences objective ('find missing numbers in an open sentence'). They sit under different Themes/Sub-Themes/Topics and share only the Grade organizer and generic stem tokens ('pupils','should','able','to','be') plus 'numbers'. There is genuine conceptual coherence: solving open sentences with a missing number relies on whole-number operations such as addition, so the two skills meaningfully reinforce one another. However, both are canonical rank 0 (PRIMARY ONE) and the evidence gives no substantive, pair-specific basis to assert a directional developmental dependency rather than complementary reinforcement, so relatesTo is the supported symmetric judgment.
